body.p: Prior to this response, claims 1-3 and 5-9 were pending. With this response, no claims are amended, added, withdrawn from consideration, or canceled. Accordingly, claims 1-3 and 5-9 remain pending. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections of the claims in view of the following remarks.

Applicant notes with appreciation the indication on pages 8 and 9 of the Office Action that claims 7-9 include allowable subject matter. Based on the below arguments, claims 7-9 depend from allowable base claims.

Claims 1-3 and 5-9 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2019/0196927 to Bosson. The rejection is traversed for at least the reasons advanced in detail below.

A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. § 102 requires every element of the claim to be included in the reference, either directly or inherently. See W.L. Gore & Assocs. v. Garlock, 721 F. 2d 1540, 220 USPQ 303 (Fed. Cir. 1983), cert. denied, 469 U.S. 851 (1984) "[a]nticipation requires the disclosure in a single prior art reference of each element of the claim under consideration." The PTO has failed to identify all elements of claim 1 as anticipated by the applied reference.

Applicant notes at the outset that the simplex Flight Control Computer as claimed in claim 1 is based on enable signals. Claim 1 (emphasis added) recites an output cutoff module receiving "enable signals generated by each monitor partition" and "the output cutoff module providing an enable signal in accordance with a predetermined enabling strategy" not found in the applied reference. Claim 1 (emphasis added) further recites "an enable switch operatively connected to the output cutoff module and to the processing unit and for providing a received signal originating from the command partition according to the enable signal."
In contrast, Bosson is based on "inhibit signals." The inhibit signals inhibit the delivery of data in the system of Bosson. The Office has failed to identify in Bosson a disclosure of the use of
the claimed enable signals in the manner claimed in claim 1. For at least this reason, claim 1 is patentable over Bosson and the rejection should be withdrawn.

Applicant also submits that the enable signals disclosed in the claimed simplex Flight Control Computer allow for consolidating the command and monitoring pairs in series and/or in parallel. In Bosson, the consolidation is performed only in series, i.e., the monitoring inhibits the command partition.

Applicant also submits that the claimed simplex Flight Control Computer considers a health validity signal for each computer in addition to the enable signal. Thus, the dual information (enable signal from the monitoring software and validity signal from the platform hardware) enables complex consolidation logic as well as provides immunity to generic hardware failures. For at least this additional reason, claim 1 is patentable over Bosson and the rejection is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.

Further, Bosson fails to disclose or render obvious the claimed "wherein the predetermined enabling strategy comprises providing a given enable signal to the enable switch to output a corresponding given received signal from the command partition when a validity signal set to valid is received from at least one given neighboring simplex flight Control Computer (FCC) as well as an enable signal set to enable is received by the monitor partition of the at least one given neighboring simplex Flight Control Computer (FCC) or when each of the at least one neighboring simplex flight control computer provides the validity signal set to invalid." (emphasis added) This feature is not implemented, disclosed, or suggested in the Bosson system.

The Office asserts that Bosson discloses the claimed feature at Figures 1-2 and paragraphs 117-120. This is incorrect because Bosson nowhere discloses an enable signal. At paragraphs 117- 120, Bosson discloses use of an inhibit signal to: prevent the delivery of output data by switch 28 and prevent the delivery of output data by switch 29. Further, Bosson at paragraphs 72-74, relied on elsewhere by the Office, also discloses that the "monitoring module 26 is configured to inhibit the delivery by the control module 24." (emphasis added) Bosson fails to disclose the use of the claimed enable signal. For at least this additional reason, claim 1 is patentable over Bosson and the rejection is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.
Further, although Bosson at paragraph 72 does state "[I]n the event of a hardware failure of the electronic computer 11," there is no disclosure of generation of a validity signal indicative

of the health of the computer. Instead, Bosson discloses the generation of an inhibition signal "to inhibit the delivery of the output data." Bosson at paragraph 81, also see paragraphs 71, 75, and 76. Bosson appears to be directed to inhibition of delivery of output data in the event of detection of an inconsistency between the result of critical functions. See Bosson at paragraphs 21, 22, 38, and 39. For at least this additional reason, claim 1 is patentable over Bosson and the rejection is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.

Further still, the Office has failed to identify any disclosure in Bosson of "when each of the at least one neighboring simplex flight control computer provides the validity signal set to invalid." The Office references Figures 1-3 and paragraphs 72-74 of Bosson for this feature; however, the Office states only that in the event of "a hardware failure of the electronic computer 11, the modules 24, 26 ... are not able to implement the critical function ... and the electronic computer 11 is in a state referred to as dysfunctional." However, there is no generation of a validity signal nor provision of a validity signal from one flight control computer to another. For at least this additional reason, claim 1 is patentable over Bosson and the rejection is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.

Further still, the Office has failed to identify in Bosson a disclosure of generating an enable signal to the enable switch to output a signal from the command partition when each of the at least one neighboring simplex flight control computer provides a validity signal set to invalid. Although relied on by the Office, there is no explanation provided by the Office or in Bosson regarding what happens if the computer 11 is in a dysfunctional state. No signal is generated. No validity signal is generated. Bosson at paragraph 72 states only that "it is likely to be detected by the monitoring module 26 of the other electronic computer 11 which is associated with the control module 24 of the electronic computer 11. (emphasis added) Thus, Bosson fails to disclose the claimed each of the at least one neighboring simplex flight control computer provides the validity signal set to invalid. For at least this additional reason, claim 1 is patentable over Bosson and the rejection is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.

Bosson discloses permanent command versus monitoring pairing between distinct electronic computers. In contrast, the claimed system enables more complex consolidation logic involving the signals from more than two electronic computers.

Further, the Bosson system requires a distinct software partition for each pairing, whereas the claimed system only requires one command and one monitoring partition per computer for any given flight controls/avionics function thereby providing a significant advantage.

Based on at least the foregoing, the claimed system is more flexible and less complicated than the Bosson system. Applicant notes that the Bosson system even refers to dynamic reallocation of the modules (see paragraph 109). Applicant respectfully submits that this is a very complicated concept avoided by the claimed system.
For at least each of these additional reasons, claim 1 is patentable over Bosson and the rejection is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.
Claims 2-3 and 5-9 depend from claim 1, include further important features, and are patentable over Bosson for at least the reasons advanced above with respect to claim 1 and/or the further features.

Because Bosson does not describe all the elements of the independent claims, either explicitly or inherently, an anticipation rejection is improper and should be withdrawn. The dependent claims are believed to be allowable at least by virtue of their dependence on the allowable independent claims, and for the additional features recited. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 102 are in order and respectfully requested.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that the present application is in condition for allowance, and such action is earnestly solicited. However, should any issue arise that may be resolved by communication with Applicant's representative, the Examiner is urged to contact the undersigned at the telephone number below to address any such issue.
